model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, Bank of Chongqing associate excluded from the flow and added at market value in the equity bridge

equity_bridge.item: Bank of Chongqing 13.48% stake at market, less 10% block discount
equity_bridge.note: ~487m shares (implied from interim note 9: 30m H shares bought = 13.48% - 12.65% of ~3,614m BOCQ shares) x 1963.HK HK$8.17 (Yahoo Finance chart API, 2026-10-16 close) = HK$3,979m, less 10% for block size, regulatory-capital treatment and the strategic (unlikely-to-be-sold) nature of the stake = 3,581. Carrying value 3,597m at 30 Jun 2026; FY2025 AR fair value 3,600m at 13.20%. The associate's profit share is excluded from every scenario's flow, so this is not double-counted. Held constant across scenarios: a BOCQ re-rating or derating moves all three by ~HK$0.25/share per HK$1 on the BOCQ H price.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (FY2020 28,441 -> FY2025 35,228); matches the base RWA/revenue growth path of 4.0% near term, 3.0% terminal (HK nominal GDP ~3.5-4%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.4% vs EPS 10.7% and revenue 8.6% (>30% apart). EPS and revenue CAGRs start from the FY2020 COVID trough (EPS 1.06, operating income 5,249) and the 2023-25 HIBOR/NIM upcycle; book growth is held down by a ~45% payout and OCI swings on the FVOCI book and the associate. EPS 3yr CAGR 15.6% is flattered by the FY2022 base (1.14, BOCQ impairments) and depressed FY2025 end-point only partly (HK$493m goodwill write-off). Equity CAGR is the better guide to sustainable compounding.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: a bank's reported FCF (OCF - capex) is deposit-flow noise. Share count flat at 1,405.75m throughout, so net income and EPS CAGRs coincide (rounding). Core profit excluding the associate: 1,398.6 (FY2024) -> 1,747.1 (FY2025, after the 493m goodwill charge; ~2,240 before it) -> 1,394 in H1 2026 alone (1,780.5 - 511.4 + 125.3). NIM 2.17% (FY2024) -> 2.41% (FY2025). Credit impairment 233m (FY2018) -> 647m (FY2020) -> 803m (FY2022) -> 1,791m (FY2024) -> 1,783m (FY2025) -> 724m (H1 2026).

scenario_narratives.base: The 2025-26 recovery holds: NIM ~2.4%, cost-to-income ~42-43%, credit cost eases from ~1.2% to ~0.9% of loans, core pre-tax margin 38% -> 40%, operating income +4% a year. CET1 stays at 19% (no capital release), so core FCFE grows from ~HK$1.4bn to ~2.6bn; the Bank of Chongqing stake is worth ~HK$2.55/share at market.
scenario_narratives.bull: HK property and loan demand recover, fees keep compounding, cost-to-income toward 40% and credit cost ~0.6%: margin 44%, growth 5-6%. The family lets CET1 drift to a peer-like 16.5%, releasing ~HK$5bn of excess capital over FY2027-30.
scenario_narratives.bear: HIBOR falls and the funding-swap cost stays wide, NIM back toward 2.1%; HK CRE and Mainland developer losses push credit cost to ~1.5% for two years; RWA inflates on downgrades with CET1 held at 19%, so FCFE collapses to ~HK$0.4bn in FY2027 and the bank earns ~6% on equity thereafter.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding its own capital requirement, discounted at the cost of equity. For Dah Sing Banking Group that flow is the CORE bank's profit (after tax and the outside AT1 coupon, excluding the equity-accounted Bank of Chongqing result) less the equity retained to hold Dah Sing Bank's CET1 ratio on growing risk-weighted assets; the Bank of Chongqing stake is valued separately at its listed H-share price less a block discount, because its accounting profit is mostly not paid out and the market capitalises it at ~0.35x book. The core bank now earns ~8-10% on equity against an 11% cost of equity, so it is worth somewhat under book; the shares at ~0.53x book and ~6x earnings price close to the bear case. The excess capital (~3pt of CET1, ~HK$3.6/share) is real but family-controlled: only the bull case counts it. Net debt is zero by construction; deposits and Tier-2 notes are operating funding.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit: HK commercial real estate (HK$23.7bn) and Mainland/HK developer exposure; credit impairment HK$1.79bn FY2024, 1.78bn FY2025, 0.72bn H1 2026. A third year at that level with no revenue growth is the bear case.
Rates: NIM 2.41% (FY2025) is a peg/HIBOR outcome as much as franchise; a renewed HIBOR collapse or a wider HKD-USD funding-swap cost reverses the 2025-26 gain.

Capital allocation: the family (via DSFH) controls the register; CET1 of 19.1% may simply keep rising, in which case minorities never see the excess - the base case already assumes no release, but a value-destructive acquisition or premises spend (Wong Chuk Hang, ~HK$1bn in H1 2026) would cost more.

Bank of Chongqing: the ~HK$2.55/share bridge item moves with a volatile Chinese city-bank H share; further CB conversions dilute the stake (13.20% -> 12.65% in H1 2026, HK$125m deemed-disposal loss) unless DSBG keeps buying back in, as it did in June 2026.
Subsidiaries: Banco Comercial de Macau (shrinking, goodwill written down HK$493m in FY2025, HK$220m goodwill left) and DSB China (credit cost above pre-provision profit) dilute group returns.
Liquidity and governance: thin free float, extensive connected transactions with DSFH/Dah Sing Insurance, auditor change PwC -> KPMG for FY2026.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (2356.HK, HKD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 10.40-15.45. Bank of Chongqing H share (1963.HK) and A share (601963.SS) from the same API, 2026-10-16 close.
data_sources.financials: 2356.HK_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized (FY2018-FY2025, H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026, HK$ millions) and kpis (NII, fees, credit impairment, cost-to-income, deposits, advances, dividends). FY2025 annual report: financial highlights (lines 1225-1245), capital and liquidity table (lines 2157-2167), income statement incl. goodwill impairment and associate share (lines 6260-6275), associate note 24 (lines 13516-13660), dividends (lines 13052-13054). H1 2026 interim: income statement (lines 70-120), balance sheet (lines 185-260), note 9 associate / deemed disposal (lines 771-805), note 10 tax, note 11 EPS (lines 874-905), note 25 AT1 (lines 1825-1860), note 35-36 CAR and leverage (lines 4680-4720), ROA/ROSF (line ~4905).
data_sources.qualitative: 2356.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-18): business model, Macau goodwill impairment, Bank of Chongqing associate, CET1 18.8%, NIM 2.41%, qualitative FY2026 guidance (no numeric targets), bull/bear cases.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E operating income, HK$ m: H1 2026 actual 4,123.3 (interim income statement line ~95, +8.6% YoY; NII 2,970 +7.0%, net fees 939 +29.2%, trading 187) + H2 2026E ~4,250 (H2 2025 actual 7,915.2 - 3,795.6 = 4,119.6, x ~1.03 on the H1 NII and fee run-rate). FY2025 actual 7,915.2 (+14.1%), FY2024 6,934.9. Operating income = NII + net fees + trading + other operating income; it EXCLUDES the share of associate (Bank of Chongqing) and jointly controlled entities, which sit below operating profit.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,405,752,132 ordinary shares, the weighted average and period-end count in every period FY2019-H1 2026 (H1 2026 interim EPS note 11, line ~880). Held FLAT: no buybacks (ShareRepurchases 0 throughout), SBC-zero, and the outstanding share options are stated to have no dilutive effect. Diluted EPS (HK$1.18 vs basic 1.27 in H1 2026) is lower ONLY because of the dilutive effect of Bank of Chongqing's convertible bonds on the associate profit share (HK$118m), not because of any DSBG share issuance; that effect is irrelevant here because the associate is valued at market price per held share, outside the flow.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: customer deposits (HK$204.6bn at 30 Jun 2026), certificates of deposit (0.29bn) and DSB's Tier-2 subordinated notes (HK$4.30bn, interest already inside interest expense and therefore inside the pre-tax margin) are operating funding / regulatory capital, not net debt. Cash and bank balances (7.4bn) are liquidity. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route; the only post-flow item is the Bank of Chongqing stake in equity_bridge.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E core FCFE, not reported OCF - capex: core profit before tax ~3,150 (H1 2026 actual 2,067.2 PBT - 511.4 share of associate + 125.3 deemed-disposal loss = 1,681.2; H2 2026E ~1,470 = revenue ~4,250 - opex ~1,800 - credit impairment ~1,000 + JCE ~20) at a 37.6% margin, less tax and external AT1 distributions at ~18% = ~2,580, LESS equity retained to lift CET1 from 18.8% on ~166.8bn RWA (FY2025) to 19.0% on ~172bn (FY2026E) = ~1,320. Reported OCF - capex (FY2025 +1,829; H1 2026 -1,288; FY2024 -2,587; FY2018 -3,058) is deposit and treasury flow noise and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: StockBasedComp 0 (or immaterial, HK$1.4m in FY2018) in Metrics.csv FY2018-H1 2026; EquityAwardTaxes 0; legacy share options outstanding but non-dilutive (H1 2026 EPS note). House and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate (band collapsed).
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Friday); valuation dated Sunday 2026-10-18
inputs.cet1_anchor: Dah Sing Bank consolidated (covering BCM Macau and DSB China), Basel III: CET1 19.1%, Tier 1 19.8%, total CAR 23.4%, leverage ratio 12.0% at 30 Jun 2026 (interim note 35-36, lines 4688-4720); CET1 18.8% / T1 19.5% / total 23.1% at FY2025 on CET1 capital HK$31,362m and 16.9% / 17.6% / 21.0% at FY2024 on 29,309m (FY2025 AR 'Capital and Liquidity' table, lines 2157-2167). Implied RWA ~HK$166.8bn FY2025 vs ~173.4bn FY2024 (RWA fell while loans grew 1.3%, so the CET1 rise is part RWA optimisation, part retained profit). HKMA minimum CET1 4.5% + 2.5% conservation buffer + countercyclical buffer + Pillar 2; DSB is not a D-SIB. The ~3pt cushion over typical HK mid-tier peers (~15-16%) is excess capital worth ~HK$5bn (~HK$3.6/share) that only the bull case releases.
inputs.ordinary_equity_anchor: Shareholders' funds HK$36,280m at 30 Jun 2026 (BVPS HK$25.81); total equity 36,592m includes HK$311m of the DSB AT1 held by DSFH (US$40m of the US$150m 11.5% AT1; the US$110m held by DSBG eliminates). Less investment in associate 3,597m, goodwill 220m and intangibles 70m = core tangible equity ~32,390m (HK$23.0/share). At current_price the stock trades at ~0.53x book and ~6x FY2026E EPS (~HK$2.3).
inputs.associate_note: Bank of Chongqing (1963.HK / 601963.SS): 13.48% at 30 Jun 2026 after buying 30m H shares on 24 Jun 2026 (interim note 9, lines 771-805), from 12.65% after BOCQ CB conversions diluted it from 13.20% (151.2m new A shares on conversion of RMB1,436.3m of its RMB13bn March-2022 6-year CB; conversion price ~RMB9.50). Implied holding: 30m = 13.48% - 12.65% of ~3,614m shares -> ~487m shares. Carrying value 3,597m (after cumulative impairment 5,447m vs share of net assets 8,055m at FY2025); fair value at the H-share close was 3,600m at FY2025 (AR note 24). Share of profit HK$729m FY2025, 677m FY2024, 511m H1 2026; dividends received only 207m (FY2025) and 288m (FY2024). Valued OUTSIDE the flow because (i) equity-accounted profit is not cash - BOCQ pays out ~30% - and (ii) the market prices BOCQ at ~0.35x book, so capitalising its earnings at our 11% CoE (~HK$9bn) would credit DSBG with value no buyer of the stake would pay.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single HKD cost of equity 11.0% in every scenario (risk charged once, through scenario weights and drivers). Built in the flows' own currency: HKD is pegged to USD, so the 10-year HKD government/Exchange Fund yield tracks the US 10-year at ~3.8-4.2% (ASSUMPTION, ~4.0% used, not fetched) + beta ~1.0 x ERP 6.0% = ~10.0%, plus 1.0pt for: controlled, thin-float register (DSFH holds the large majority), sub-scale second-tier HK franchise, HK CRE (HK$23.7bn) and Mainland developer concentration. Consistent with the house's HK/China bank range (0998.HK 10.5% and 2016.HK 11.0% on CNY rates ~2pt lower; 1658.HK). Hurdle for entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation (ROU assets 328m FY2025) and lease interest sit inside operating expenses and so inside the pre-tax margin. lease_cost_pct_path is zero so the charge is not taken twice; lease liabilities are not deducted as debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: No ordinary minority interests (profit for the period is 100% attributable to shareholders). The only outside claim is the DSFH-held US$40m of DSB's 11.5% AT1 (HK$311m in total equity; distributions ~HK$36m a year, H1 2026 17.98m, interim line 369). It is charged once, inside the 'cash_tax_rate' deduction (~1.1pt of core PBT), and not deducted again in a bridge. Call date 8 Dec 2027; if not called it resets to 5y UST + 788bp (~11.8%), immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (0998.HK, 2016.HK, 1658.HK, HSBC, LYG, NAB.AX). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF swings between -3.1bn and +10.3bn, net debt is zero by construction. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = operating income; ebitda_margin = CORE pre-tax margin (after credit impairment, the real cost of a bank; includes the small JCE share; EXCLUDES the Bank of Chongqing share of results, deemed-disposal losses, associate impairments and the FY2025 HK$493m Macau goodwill write-off); SBC, D&A, leases and working capital zero; cash_tax_rate = income tax + external AT1 distributions, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = core profit to ordinary shareholders; capex = equity retained to hold DSB's CET1 ratio at the scenario target on RWA growth (target_t x RWA_t - target_t-1 x RWA_t-1, as % of revenue, from FY2026E RWA HK$172bn), so FCF = core FCFE. Terminal-decade RWA growth equals terminal growth so the terminal FCFE is self-consistent. The Bank of Chongqing stake is added once, at market value less a 10% block discount, in equity_bridge (all scenarios). The 18x terminal cap does not bind (Gordon 12.9x base, 13.8x bull, 12.1x bear). KEY FINDINGS: (1) The core bank is earning ~8% on core tangible equity (FY2026E ~2.58bn on ~32.4bn) and ~10% group-wide (H1 2026 annualised ROSF 10.0%), up from 6.2% (FY2024) on a 24bp NIM gain to 2.41% and a cost-to-income fall from 48.2% to 42.5% (H1 2026); credit cost (~1.2% of loans, HK$1.78bn in both FY2024 and FY2025, 724m in H1 2026) is the single largest drag and the swing factor. (2) CET1 19.1% is ~3pt above HK mid-tier peers; dividends (HK$0.80 FY2025 +21%, interim 0.35 vs 0.31) are roughly 45-50% of profit, so FCFE at a 19% CET1 is close to the dividend actually paid. The base case does NOT release the excess capital - a family-controlled bank that calls itself prudent has shown no sign of buybacks - only the bull does (glide to 16.5%). (3) The stock at ~0.53x book and ~6x earnings sits just above the bear value; the base needs only that credit costs stop rising. DRIVER EVIDENCE: FY2025 annual (financial highlights lines 1225-1245: operating income 7,915.2, PBT 2,859.6, NIM 2.41%, C/I 43.5%; capital table lines 2157-2167; associate note 24 lines 13516-13660; goodwill impairment line 6265; DPS 0.31 + 0.49) and H1 2026 interim (income statement lines 70-120; balance sheet lines 185-260; note 9 associate; note 25 AT1; note 35 CAR; ROA 1.4% / ROSF 10.0% line ~4905). Management gives no numeric FY2026 guidance (qualitative: 'cautiously optimistic', CRE demand 'somewhat positive', residential recovery continuing). Valuation date is 9.5 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027. The H1 2026 premises spend (Wong Chuk Hang acquisition; premises + investment property up ~HK$0.96bn, capex line 1,110m) is a one-off already inside the fy0 balance sheet and is not projected.

bear.growth_rationale: HIBOR falls with further Fed cuts and the HKD-USD funding-swap cost stays wide: NIM gives back the 2025 gain toward ~2.1%, treasury income weakens, loan book flat; operating income falls two years before growing with nominal GDP.
bear.margin_rationale: HK CRE (HK$23.7bn book) and Mainland developer losses step up again - credit cost ~1.5% of loans for two years - on a smaller revenue line; Macau and DSB China stay loss-adjacent. Margin troughs at the FY2024 level (24.8%) only partly, recovering to ~34% (FY2025's 33.2%).
bear.capex_rationale: CET1 held at 19.0% while CRE downgrades inflate RWA 5% in FY2027 despite falling revenue, then RWA grows 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5%. Retention HK$1.63bn in FY2027 eats most of a ~HK$2.05bn core profit (FCFE ~0.4bn, i.e. the dividend is cut or paid from the buffer), then ~HK$0.7-1.2bn. Terminal core ROE ~6%, implied P/B ~0.45x.
bear.tax_rationale: AT1 coupon fixed against a smaller PBT; Mainland/Macau losses not tax-shielded at group level.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon 1.025/0.085 = 12.1x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bear.narrative: NIM unwinds as HIBOR falls, CRE losses return, RWA inflates on downgrades; the family keeps CET1 at 19% so distributions shrink and the bank earns ~6% on equity indefinitely.

base.growth_rationale: Operating income +4% a year, the pace of the balance sheet: loans ~+2% in H1 2026 with HK loan demand recovering off a low base (residential prices +3.3% in 2025, CRE demand 'somewhat positive'), fee income still compounding from the Sun Life bancassurance and private-banking build (+29% H1 2026) but slowing from that rate, NIM held near 2.4% (HKMA sector NIM recovering in H1 2026, but limited room for further prime cuts cuts both ways). Fades to 3% = HK nominal growth.
base.margin_rationale: Core pre-tax margin (ex associate, ex goodwill): FY2024 24.8% (1,718/6,935), FY2025 33.2% (2,624/7,915), H1 2025 36.2%, H2 2025 30.3%, H1 2026 40.8%, FY2026E ~37.6% (H2 seasonally heavier provisioning). Base drifts to 40%: cost-to-income holds ~42-43% and credit cost eases from ~1.2% of loans toward ~0.9% as the HK CRE cycle stops deteriorating. Each 0.1pt of credit cost on ~HK$145bn of loans is ~1.7pt of margin. No further NIM gain assumed.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold DSB's CET1 FLAT at 19.0% (status quo; no release of the ~3pt excess) on RWA growth of 4.0% for five years, 3.5% for two, then 3.0%, from FY2026E RWA HK$172bn. Retention = 0.19 x delta RWA: HK$1.31bn FY2027 rising to 1.53bn FY2031, 1.36bn FY2036; / revenue = 15.0% falling to 11.4%. FCFE FY2027 ~HK$1.4bn (~HK$1.00/share), close to the current ~HK$0.85 dividend. Terminal RWA ~HK$245bn, CET1 capital ~46.5bn, terminal core ROE ~8.5%, implied core P/B ~0.7x.
base.tax_rationale: HK profits tax 16.5%; H1 2026 tax 286.8m on core PBT 1,681 = 17.1% (Mainland/Macau tax and deferred tax on top of HK); plus DSFH's AT1 distributions ~36m/yr (~1.1pt). Pillar Two noted but no top-up charged to date (interim note 10).
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 11.0% - 3.0% = 12.9x; 18x cap does not bind. Implied terminal core P/B ~0.7x on ~8.5% ROE, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g).
base.narrative: Status quo: the 2025-26 recovery holds, credit cost eases toward 0.9% of loans, the bank grows with HK at ~4% and keeps CET1 at 19% - minorities get roughly the dividend they get today, growing.

bull.growth_rationale: HK property and loan demand recover properly (rate cuts, Mainland buyers, Northern Metropolis), CNH lending and cross-border/GBA wealth keep fee income growing double digits for two more years, NIM holds 2.4%+ on CASA mix.
bull.margin_rationale: Cost-to-income toward 40% on operating leverage (digital/paperless branch programme) and credit cost back to ~0.6% of loans as CRE stress clears; 44% is a little above the H1 2026 run-rate of 40.8%.
bull.capex_rationale: Excess capital released: CET1 glides 19.0% -> 18.4 -> 17.8 -> 17.2 -> 16.6% (FY2027-30) then held at 16.5%, still well above HKMA requirements and in line with HK peers, while RWA grows 5.0% for five years then 4.5, 4.0, 4.0, 3.5, 3.5%. Retention ~HK$0.46-0.55bn a year during the glide (the release funds higher payouts or buybacks), then ~HK$1.4-1.6bn. Terminal core ROE ~10%.
bull.tax_rationale: AT1 distribution shrinks as a share of a larger PBT (or the AT1 is called Dec 2027).
bull.terminal_note: Gordon 1.035/0.075 = 13.8x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bull.narrative: HK recovery plus capital release: margin to 44%, growth 5-6%, and the family lets CET1 drift to a peer-like 16.5%, handing ~HK$5bn of excess capital to shareholders over four years.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (above the 15% house default): HK CRE is in what management calls one of its most challenging periods for years, credit charges have run at ~HK$1.8bn for two straight years, Macau needed a goodwill write-off and DSB China's credit cost exceeds its pre-provision profit; HK NIM is a function of the Fed via the peg. Offsetting this, the 19.1% CET1 means the bear is an earnings problem, not a solvency or dilution one - hence below the 35-40% used for the thinly capitalised Chinese joint-stock banks. Bull 20%: needs both an HK credit recovery and a change in a conservative family's capital-return behaviour, of which there is so far only a dividend-raise hint (+21% FY2025, +13% interim). Base 50%: H1 2026 core profit +23% and flat impairments say the improvement is real.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
